title: What If the Solar Wind Blew Earth's Atmosphere Into Space?
description:
What Happens When Earth's Magnetic Field Flips?

What if the solar wind blew Earth's atmosphere into space during a magnetic flip? Even when Earth's main dipole weakens to about a tenth of its normal strength, smaller poles remain and the nitrogen and oxygen above our heads weigh as much as a 10-metre layer of water — while a flip takes only a few thousand years compared with billions of years on smaller, lower-gravity Mars.

Sources: NASA Science, Flip Flop: Why Variations in Earth's Magnetic Field Aren't Causing Today's Climate Change — reversals, residual field and fossil record (https://science.nasa.gov/science-research/earth-science/flip-flop-why-variations-in-earths-magnetic-field-arent-causing-todays-climate-change/) · British Geological Survey, Reversals — the liquid outer core and atmospheric shielding (https://geomag.bgs.ac.uk/education/reversals.html).

Pictures: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio (SVS 3822, SVS 12312, SVS 20297), NASA/ISS HDEV, NASA/NOAA/GSFC/Suomi NPP VIIRS (GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001788), and NASA/JPL/USGS Viking Orbiter Mars (PIA00407) alongside original animated explainers, with AI-assisted voice and editing. Facts: every number is checked against the sources listed above.
Image credits: NASA/GSFC Scientific Visualization Studio (Bailee DesRocher, Genna Duberstein, Eric Christian, Greg Shirah, Tom Bridgman, Michael Starobin, Kayvon Sharghi, Joycelyn Thomson Jones, Jay Herman, Adam Szabo, Alexander Marshak); NASA/ISS High Definition Earth-Viewing (HDEV) experiment; NASA/NOAA/GSFC/Suomi NPP/VIIRS/Norman Kuring (GSFC_20171208_Archive_e001788); NASA/JPL/USGS (PIA00407).
